   693→    def parse_options(self, extra):
   694→        """Parse the command line arguments for the Command.
   695→
   696→        After the initial ArgumentParser runs to choose the Command for the selected
   697→        platform and format, a new ArgumentParser is created here to parse the remaining
   698→        command line arguments specific to the Command. Additionally, the default
   699→        options for disabling input, log verbosity, and log saving are parsed out and
   700→        saved to the Command.
   701→
   702→        :param extra: the remaining command line arguments after the initial
   703→            ArgumentParser runs over the command line.
   704→        :return: dictionary of parsed arguments for Command, and a dictionary of parsed
   705→            configuration overrides.
   706→        """
   707→        default_format = getattr(
   708→            get_platforms().get(self.platform), "DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FORMAT", None
   709→        )
   710→        # only show supported formats for Commands that support formats
   711→        if default_format is not None and self.command not in {"new", "dev", "upgrade"}:
   712→            formats = list(get_output_formats(self.platform).keys())
   713→            formats[formats.index(default_format)] = f"{default_format} (default)"
   714→            supported_formats_helptext = (
   715→                f"Supported formats:\n  {', '.join(sorted(formats, key=str.lower))}"
   716→            )
   717→        else:
   718→            supported_formats_helptext = ""
   719→
   720→        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   721→            prog=self.cmd_line.format(
   722→                command=self.command,
   723→                platform=self.platform,
   724→                output_format=self.output_format,
   725→            ),
   726→            description=self.console.textwrap(
   727→                f"{self.description}\n\n{supported_formats_helptext}"
   728→            ),
   729→            formatter_class=(
   730→                lambda prog: RawDescriptionHelpFormatter(prog, width=MAX_TEXT_WIDTH)
   731→            ),
   732→        )
   733→
   734→        self.add_default_options(parser)
   735→        self.add_options(parser)
   736→
   737→        # If the command allows passthrough arguments, add an option for the help,
   738→        # then process the argument list to strip out the passthrough args.
   739→        if self.allows_passthrough:
   740→            parser.add_argument(
   741→                "--",
   742→                dest="passthrough",
   743→                metavar="ARGS ...",
   744→                required=False,
   745→                help="Arguments to pass to the app",
   746→            )
   747→            args, passthrough = split_passthrough(extra)
   748→        else:
   749→            args = extra
   750→
   751→        # Parse the full set of command line options from the content
   752→        # remaining after the basic command/platform/output format
   753→        # has been extracted.
   754→        options = vars(parser.parse_args(args))
   755→
   756→        if self.allows_passthrough:
   757→            options["passthrough"] = passthrough
   758→
   759→        # Extract the base default options onto the command
   760→        self.console.input_enabled = options.pop("input_enabled")
   761→        self.console.verbosity = options.pop("verbosity")
   762→        self.console.save_log = options.pop("save_log")
   763→
   764→        # Parse the configuration overrides
   765→        overrides = parse_config_overrides(options.pop("config_overrides"))
   766→
   767→        return options, overrides

   926→    def update_cookiecutter_cache(self, template: str, branch="master"):
   927→        """Ensure that we have a current checkout of a template path.
   928→
   929→        If the path is a local path, use the path as is.
   930→
   931→        If the path is a URL, look for a local cache; if one exists, update it,
   932→        including checking out the required branch.
   933→
   934→        :param template: The template URL or path.
   935→        :param branch: The template branch to use. Default: ``master``
   936→        :return: The path to the cached template. This may be the originally
   937→            provided path if the template was a file path.
   938→        """
   939→        if is_repo_url(template):
   940→            # The app template is a repository URL.
   941→            #
   942→            # Look for a Briefcase cache of the template.
   943→            cached_template = self.template_cache_path(template)
   944→
   945→            if cached_template.exists():
   946→                # There is a pre-existing cache of the template. Attempt to update it;
   947→                # if the fetch fails, use the existing state of the cache. Any other
   948→                # failure is surfaced to the user.
   949→                try:
   950→                    repo = self.tools.git.Repo(cached_template)
   951→                except self.tools.git.exc.GitError:
   952→                    # Template repository is in a weird state. Delete it
   953→                    self.console.warning(
   954→                        "Template cache is in a weird state. Getting a clean clone."
   955→                    )
   956→                    self.tools.shutil.rmtree(cached_template)
   957→
   958→            if not cached_template.exists():
   959→                # There's no pre-existing template. It's either the first time seeing
   960→                # the template, or the template was in a weird state. Perform a blobless
   961→                # clone.
   962→                try:
   963→                    self.console.info(f"Cloning template {template!r}...")
   964→                    cached_template.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)
   965→                    repo = self.tools.git.Repo.clone_from(
   966→                        url=template,
   967→                        to_path=cached_template,
   968→                        filter=["blob:none"],
   969→                        no_checkout=True,
   970→                    )

   106→def ensure_console_is_safe(sub_method):
   107→    """Decorator for Subprocess methods to conditionally remove dynamic console elements
   108→    such as the Wait Bar prior to running the subprocess command.
   109→

   111→    """
   112→
   113→    @wraps(sub_method)
   114→    def inner(sub: Subprocess, args: SubprocessArgsT, *wrapped_args, **wrapped_kwargs):
   115→        """Evaluate whether conditions are met to remove any dynamic elements in the
   116→        console before returning control to Subprocess.
   117→
   118→        :param sub: Bound Subprocess object
   119→        :param args: command line to run in subprocess
   120→        :returns: the return value for the Subprocess method
   121→        """
   122→        # Just run the command if no dynamic elements are active
   123→        if not sub.tools.console.is_console_controlled:
   124→            return sub_method(sub, args, *wrapped_args, **wrapped_kwargs)
   125→
   126→        remove_dynamic_elements = False
   127→
   128→        # Batch (.bat) scripts on Windows.
   129→        # If cmd.exe is interrupted with CTRL+C while running a bat script,
   130→        # it may prompt the user to abort the script and dynamic elements
   131→        # such as the Wait Bar can hide this message from the user.
   132→        if sub.tools.host_os == "Windows":
   133→            executable = str(args[0]).strip() if args else ""
   134→            remove_dynamic_elements |= executable.lower().endswith(".bat")
   135→
   136→        # Release control for commands that cannot be streamed.
   137→        remove_dynamic_elements |= wrapped_kwargs.get("stream_output") is False
   138→
   139→        # Run subprocess command with or without console control
   140→        if remove_dynamic_elements:
   141→            with sub.tools.console.release_console_control():
   142→                return sub_method(sub, args, *wrapped_args, **wrapped_kwargs)
   143→        else:
   144→            return sub_method(sub, args, *wrapped_args, **wrapped_kwargs)
   145→
   146→    return inner

   183→                # The stop_flag is intentionally checked both at the top and bottom of
   184→                # this loop; if the flag was set during the call to readline(), then
   185→                # processing the output is skipped altogether. And if the flag is set
   186→                # as a consequence of filter_func(), the streamer still exits before
   187→                # calling readline() again and potentially blocking indefinitely.
   188→                if not self.stop_flag.is_set():

   190→
   191→                    for filtered_line in filtered_output:
   192→                        if self.capture_output:
   193→                            self.output_queue.put_nowait(filtered_line)
   194→                        else:
   195→                            self.console.info(filtered_line)

   197→                    if stop_streaming:
   198→                        self.stop_flag.set()
   199→
   200→                if self.stop_flag.is_set():
   201→                    break

   421→    def run(
   422→        self,
   423→        args: SubprocessArgsT,
   424→        stream_output: bool = True,
   425→        filter_func: Callable[[str], Iterator[str]] | None = None,
   426→        **kwargs,
   427→    ) -> CompletedProcess:
   428→        """A wrapper for subprocess.run().
   429→
   430→        This method implements the behavior of subprocess.run() with some notable
   431→        differences:
   432→
   433→          - The command's output is streamed if ``stream_output=True`` or if dynamic
   434→            console content such as the Wait Bar is active and I/O is not redirected.
   435→          - If dynamic content is not active, ``stream_output=False`` will disable
   436→            streaming.
   437→          - If the ``env`` argument is provided, the current system environment will be
   438→            copied, and the contents of env overwritten into that environment.
   439→          - The ``text`` argument is defaulted to True so all output is returned as
   440→            strings instead of bytes.
   441→
   442→        Output Streaming Primer
   443→        ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
   444→
   445→        What is output streaming?
   446→        -------------------------
   447→
   448→        When a command is invoked via ``subprocess.run()``, by default, its stdout and
   449→        stderr are connected directly to the console and the output is presented to the
   450→        user as though the command was invoked natively. When output streaming is
   451→        active, Briefcase reads the command's output and prints it in to the console on
   452→        behalf of the command.
   453→
   454→        Why is output streaming necessary?
   455→        ----------------------------------
   456→
   457→        Allowing commands to print directly to the console can provide superior UX since
   458→        it allows tools to provide their native experience to users.
   459→
   460→        However, a primary mechanism for providing support for Briefcase is asking users
   461→        to provide the log file when errors occur. Often, these errors are raised by
   462→        invoked commands; streaming the output of commands allows Briefcase to capture
   463→        that output and include it in the log file as well as the console.
   464→
   465→        Additionally, the content of the console can become corrupted if other processes
   466→        print to the console while Rich's dynamic console elements such as a Progress
   467→        Bar are active. Streaming such output allows Rich to maintain integrity of all
   468→        the console content.
   469→
   470→        How does output streaming work?
   471→        -------------------------------
   472→
   473→        Streaming is activated when:
   474→
   475→          1. dynamic content such as the Wait Bar is active and I/O is not redirected
   476→
   477→          2. the ``stream_output`` argument is ``True`` (as it is by default)
   478→
   479→        I/O is considered redirected when both ``stdout`` and ``stderr`` are specified
   480→        (e.g., when ``stdout`` and ``stderr`` are set to``subprocess.PIPE`` so the
   481→        output is available to the caller).
   482→
   483→        To facilitate streaming the output, ``stdout`` is set to ``subprocess.PIPE``. If
   484→        ``stderr`` is not specified by calling code, then it is set to
   485        ``subprocess.STDOUT`` so it is interlaced with stdout output.
   486→
   487→        The process is created for the command with ``Popen``, and a separate thread is
   488→        started for continuously reading and printing the stdout to the console from the
   489→        command process. It is necessary to read from stdout in a thread because the
   490→        read is uninterruptible; so, a user may not be able to abort with CTRL-C.
   491→
   492→        When the process ends (or the user sends CTRL-C), a call is made to ensure the
   493→        command process terminates; this, in turn, ensures the thread for streaming can
   494→        properly exit its otherwise infinite loop. The calling code is either returned a
   495→        ``CompletedProcess`` object or ``CalledProcessError`` could be raised.
   496→
   497→        Output streaming ultimately strives to simulate calling ``subprocess.run()``
   498→        while proxying the command's output to the console.
   499→
   500→        When *not* to use output streaming?
   501→        -----------------------------------
   502→
   503→        When streaming is disabled, the command's output **WILL NOT** be included the
   504→        Briefcase log file. This makes troubleshooting difficult and should be avoided.
   505→        However, there are some situations where disabling streaming is unavoidable.
   506→
   507→        Some commands use their own dynamic console content such as progress bars,
   508→        spinners, and other animations. When such output is streamed, its quality can be
   509→        significantly compromised and look terrible in the console for users. If it is
   510→        not possible to disable such output with e.g. a flag for the command, then
   511→        disabling streaming may be necessary. As an example, the ``flatpak install``
   512→        command uses many animations.
   513→
   514→        If a command requires user input, do not use output streaming. The output
   515→        streaming implementation doesn't provide any facilities to send input to the
   516→        process and doesn't provide any special handling of stdin. Additionally, when
   517→        the command process prompts the user for input, that doesn't always trigger
   518→        ``readline()`` to return; so, the console may actually end up waiting for user
   519→        input before displaying a prompt to the user. As an example, accepting Android
   520→        SDK licenses requires user input.
   521→
   522→        :param args: args for ``subprocess.run()``
   523→        :param stream_output: simulate ``run()`` while streaming the output to the
   524→            console. Set to False if the command requires user interaction.
   525→        :param filter_func: If output streaming is enabled, a callable that will be
   526→            invoked on every line of output that is streamed. The function accepts the
   527→            "raw" line of input (stripped of any trailing newline); it returns a
   528→            generator that yields the filtered output that should be displayed to the
   529→            user. Can raise StopStreaming to terminate the output stream.
   530→        :param kwargs: keyword args for ``subprocess.run()``
   531→        :raises ValueError: if a filter function is provided when in non-streaming mode.
   532→        :returns: ``CompletedProcess`` for invoked process
   533→        """
   534→
   535→        # Stream the output unless the caller explicitly disables it. When a
   536→        # caller sets stream_output=False, then ensure_console_is_safe() will
   537→        # disable any dynamic console elements while the command runs.
   538→        if stream_output:
   539→            return self._run_and_stream_output(args, filter_func=filter_func, **kwargs)
   540→
   541→        # Can't filter non-streamed output.
   542→        if filter_func:
   543→            raise ValueError("Cannot apply a filter to non-streamed output.")
   544→
   545→        # Otherwise, invoke run() normally.
   546→        self._log_command(args)
   547→        self._log_cwd(kwargs.get("cwd"))
   548→        self._log_environment(kwargs.get("env"))
   549→
   550→        try:
   551→            command_result = self._subprocess.run(
   552→                [str(arg) for arg in args], **self.final_kwargs(**kwargs)
   553→            )
   554→        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
   555→            self._log_return_code(e.returncode)
   556→            raise
   557→        self._log_return_code(command_result.returncode)
   558→
   559→        return command_result

   561→    def _run_and_stream_output(
   562→        self,
   563→        args: SubprocessArgsT,
   564→        check: bool = False,
   565→        filter_func: Callable[[str], Iterator[str]] | None = None,
   566→        **kwargs,
   567→    ) -> CompletedProcess:
   568→        """Simulate subprocess.run() while streaming output to the console.
   569→
   570→        This is useful when dynamic screen content is active or output should
   571→        be captured for logging.
   572→
   573→        When dynamic screen content like a Wait Bar is active, output can
   574→        only be printed to the screen via Console to avoid interfering
   575→        with and likely corrupting the updates to the dynamic screen elements.
   576→
   577→        stdout will always be piped so it can be printed to the screen;
   578→        however, stderr can be piped by the caller so it is available
   579→        to the caller in the return value...as with subprocess.run().
   580→
   581→        Note: the 'timeout' and 'input' arguments are not supported.
   582→        """
   583→        if kwargs.get("stdout") and not kwargs.get("stderr"):
   584→            # This is an unsupported configuration, as it's not clear where stderr
   585→            # output would be displayed. Either:
   586→            # * Redirect stderr in addition to stdout; or
   587→            # * Use check_output() instead of run() to capture console output
   588→            #   without streaming.
   589→            raise AssertionError(
   590→                "Subprocess.run() was invoked while dynamic Rich content is active (or via "
   591→                "`stream_output`) with stdout redirected while stderr was not redirected."
   592→            )
   593→        for arg in [arg for arg in ["timeout", "input"] if arg in kwargs]:
   594→            raise AssertionError(
   595→                f"The Subprocess.run() '{arg}' argument is not supported "
   596→                f"with `stream_output` or while dynamic Rich content is active."
   597→            )
   598→
   599→        # stdout must be piped so the output streamer can print it.
   600→        kwargs["stdout"] = subprocess.PIPE
   601→        # if stderr isn't explicitly redirected, then send it to stdout.
   602→        kwargs.setdefault("stderr", subprocess.STDOUT)
   603→        # use line-buffered output by default
   604→        kwargs.setdefault("bufsize", 1)
   605→
   606→        stderr = None
   607→        with self.Popen(args, **kwargs) as process:
   608→            self.stream_output(args[0], process, filter_func=filter_func)
   609→            if process.stderr and kwargs["stderr"] != subprocess.STDOUT:
   610→                stderr = process.stderr.read()
   611→        return_code = process.poll()
   612→        self._log_return_code(return_code)
   613→
   614→        if check and return_code:
   615→            raise subprocess.CalledProcessError(return_code, args, stderr=stderr)
   616→
   617→        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, return_code, stderr=stderr)

   619→    @ensure_console_is_safe
   620→    def check_output(self, args: SubprocessArgsT, quiet: int = 0, **kwargs) -> str:
   621→        """A wrapper for subprocess.check_output()
   622→
   623→        The behavior of this method is identical to subprocess.check_output(), except
   624→        for:
   625→         - If the `env` is argument provided, the current system environment will be
   626→           copied, and the contents of env overwritten into that environment.
   627→         - The `text` argument is defaulted to True so all output is returned as strings
   628→           instead of bytes.
   629→         - The `stderr` argument is defaulted to `stdout` so _all_ output is returned
   630→           and `stderr` isn't unexpectedly printed to the console.
   631→
   632→        :param args: commands and its arguments to run via subprocess
   633→        :param quiet: Should the invocation of this command be silent, and *not* appear
   634→            in the logs? This should almost always be 0, indicating "not quiet"; any
   635→            command output will be logged, and any errors will be logged *and* printed
   636→            to the console. A value of 1 will log all command output, but errors will be
   637→            logged, but *not* printed to the console. A value of 2 will *not* log any
   638→            command output; errors will be logged, but *not* printed to the console. A
   639→            value of 2 is mostly useful for calls that are called frequently to evaluate
   640→            the status of another process (such as calls that poll an API) so that log
   641→            output isn't corrupted by thousands of polling calls.
   642→        """
   643→        # if stderr isn't explicitly redirected, then send it to stdout.
   644→        kwargs.setdefault("stderr", subprocess.STDOUT)
   645→
   646→        if quiet < 2:
   647→            self._log_command(args)
   648→            self._log_cwd(kwargs.get("cwd"))
   649→            self._log_environment(kwargs.get("env"))
   650→
   651→        try:
   652→            cmd_output = self._subprocess.check_output(
   653→                [str(arg) for arg in args], **self.final_kwargs(**kwargs)
   654→            )
   655→        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
   656→            # Subprocess errors will be logged, and also printed to console if we're at
   657→            # DEBUG+ log levels. However, if we're at quiet=0 *and* a non-debug log
   658→            # level, we need to explicitly output to the console.
   659→            if quiet == 0 and self.tools.console.verbosity < LogLevel.DEBUG:
   660→                self.output_error(e)
   661→            if quiet < 2:
   662→                self._log_output(e.output, e.stderr)
   663→                self._log_return_code(e.returncode)
   664→            raise
   665→
   666→        if quiet < 2:
   667→            self._log_output(cmd_output)
   668→            self._log_return_code(0)
   669→        return cmd_output

   730→    def stream_output(
   731→        self,
   732→        label: str,
   733→        popen_process: subprocess.Popen,
   734→        stop_func: Callable[[], bool] = lambda: False,
   735→        filter_func: Callable[[str], Iterator[str]] | None = None,
   736→    ):
   737→        """Stream the output of a Popen process until the process exits. If the user
   738→        sends CTRL+C, the process will be terminated.
   739→
   740→        This is useful for starting a process via Popen such as tailing a log file, then
   741→        initiating a non-blocking process that populates that log, and finally streaming
   742→        the original process's output here.
   743→
   744→        :param label: A description of the content being streamed; used for to provide
   745→            context in logging messages.
   746→        :param popen_process: a running Popen process with output to print
   747→        :param stop_func: A Callable that returns True when output streaming should stop
   748→            and the popen_process should be terminated.
   749→        :param filter_func: A callable that will be invoked on every line of output that
   750→            is streamed. The function accepts the "raw" line of input (stripped of any
   751→            trailing newline); it returns a generator that yields the filtered output
   752→            that should be displayed to the user. Can raise StopStreaming to terminate
   753→            the output stream.
   754→        """
   755→        output_streamer = PopenOutputStreamer(
   756→            label=label,
   757→            popen_process=popen_process,
   758→            console=self.tools.console,
   759→            filter_func=filter_func,
   760→        )
   761→        try:
   762→            output_streamer.start()
   763→            # joining the thread is avoided due to demonstrated
   764→            # instability of thread interruption via CTRL+C (#809)
   765→            while not stop_func() and output_streamer.is_alive():
   766→                time.sleep(0.1)
   767→        except KeyboardInterrupt:
   768→            self.tools.console.info("Stopping...")
   769→            # allow time for CTRL+C to propagate to the child process
   770→            time.sleep(0.25)
   771→            # re-raise to exit as "Aborted by user"
   772→            raise
   773→        finally:
   774→            self.cleanup(label, popen_process)
   775→            streamer_deadline = time.time() + 3
   776→            while output_streamer.is_alive() and time.time() < streamer_deadline:
   777→                time.sleep(0.1)
   778→            if output_streamer.is_alive():
   779→                self.tools.console.error(
   780→                    "Log stream hasn't terminated; log output may be corrupted."
   781→                )
